title: Sections-tensor comparison commutes with shifts
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and finite extensions $E\subseteq L$ of $\Ql$ inside $\Qlb$ with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subseteq\mathcal O_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $R_F=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,s}$ for $F=E,L$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $K\in D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Apply exact sections over the final object of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ termwise [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], with the canonical constant-value maps $\mathcal O_F\to\Gamma(s,R_F)=\varprojlim_n\Gamma(s,(\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n)_s)$ [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] sending $b$ to the compatible family of its constant sections. Let
$$
 \theta_K:\Gamma(s,K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\longrightarrow\Gamma(s,K\otimes^L_{R_E}R_L)
$$
be the canonical sections-tensor comparison specified in [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension], where tensor on the left is ordinary tensor of module complexes and on the right is ordinary derived change of sheaf rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] along the canonical map $R_E\to R_L$ induced by $\mathcal O_E\subseteq\mathcal O_L$ [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. For every $m\in\mathbf Z$, $\theta_{K[m]}=\theta_K[m]$ under the standard termwise shift identifications for sections and scalar tensor; these identifications are compatible with zero and successive shifts.

Explicitly, on a K-flat resolution $P\to K$ with flat terms [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], the representing map in degree $r$ is
$$
 \Gamma(s,P^r)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\longrightarrow\Gamma(s,P^r\otimes_{R_E}R_L),\qquad a\otimes b\longmapsto\text{the sheaf tensor section }a\otimes b_s,
$$
where $b_s\in R_L(s)$ is the constant section defined by $b$ and the sheaf tensor is [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. These maps form a natural map of complexes, commute with the standard integer shifts, and induce the displayed equality in $D(\mathcal O_L)$ independently of the chosen resolution.

proof.text: The proved source-library instances CategoryTheory.NatTrans.commShift_mapHomologicalComplex, CategoryTheory.Functor.commShift_mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_hom and CategoryTheory.Functor.commShift_mapDerivedCategoryCompIso_hom show that the termwise comparison and the exact-functor composition comparisons commute with integer shifts. Functor.CommShift.ofIso_compatibility makes the inverse ordinary derived comparison commute with the shift transported independently of theta. Whiskering and composing these compatibilities proves the displayed derived shift square and the chain-level square. Zero and addition coherence are those of the existing CommShift structures.

proof.text: For any representative isomorphism e, naturality of pointDerivedSectionsTensor moves e.hom across the comparison. Functoriality and e.hom followed by e.inv equal to the identity cancel its transport. Expand the source and target factorization isomorphisms and the definition of pointDerivedSectionsTensor. Cancel the ordinary derived comparison and its inverse, followed by the target composition comparison and its inverse. The remaining identity is precisely Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_fac applied to pointSectionsTensor and P. This proves the representative formula for every complex and every e, hence in particular for all K-flat flat-term representatives, independently of the choice.
